El diagnóstico es anterior a la cura. En: The diagnosis came before the cure. In 1991 Sepp Hochreiter analysed in his diploma thesis, in German and without much impact, why recurrent networks did not learn long dependencies, and hit on the exact answer: the vanishing product of factors. Six years later, in 1997, he published with Jürgen Schmidhuber the architecture that dodged it, the LSTM, whose name means long short-term memory. It took another good decade to catch on, because it needed data and machines that did not exist then. It is a clear case of understanding well why something fails being half the work.

Entre 1997 y aproximadamente 2017, las L: Between 1997 and roughly 2017, LSTMs were what there was for anything that was a sequence: speech recognition on phones, machine translation, time series prediction, text generation. Google put them into its translator in 2016 with a very visible improvement on what came before. Today in text they have been displaced by transformers, but they are still alive where the sequence arrives item by item and you have to answer on the fly without being able to look at the future: sensors, control, real-time signals and small devices where nothing bigger fits.
